messages.subject: [relogit] Re: RELOGIT package
messages.body_plain:
calculating R^2 and fit statistics in general doesn't make sense for 
comparing relogit and logit.  Logit will fit better, but relogit will be 
less biased.  In almost all applications its bias rather than fit that 
we're shooting for.  its the same for comparing OLS and WLS by the way: 
WLS will never fit better than OLS (which after all is _least_ squares) 
but if done properly WLS will have better statistical properties.

Best,
Gary

messages.subject: [relogit] Re: RELOGIT package
messages.body_plain:
but that's the issue.  the fit is 'worse' in relogit, just as the fit is 
worse in WLS, but 'worse' in these cases means 'better'.  so if you did 
out of sample prediction, relogit or wls would do better than logit or 
ols, respectively (under the right conditions of course).  in WLS, R^2 
needn't even be between 0 and 1, which basically means that its not at all 
clear what the quantity you're calculating should be.  same in relogit. 
so set aside some of the data and predict if you want, or do more formal 
cross-validation, but i don't think you want R^2, even if we knew what it 
was.

and as a side point, you probably don't even want R^2 in regression for 
most purposes.  see for example:  Gary King. "How Not to Lie With 
Statistics: Avoiding Common Mistakes in Quantitative Political Science," 
American Journal of Political Science, Vol. 30, No. 3 (August, 1986): Pp. 
666-687, copy at http://gking.harvard.edu/files/abs/mist-abs.shtml.

Gary
